references.text: Moses blesses the tribes of Israel before his death, parallel to Jacob's blessings of his sons.
Balaam uses the expression 'in the last days' (באחרית הימים) when he prophesies about what will happen to Moab, parallel to Jacob's use of the same expression.
Moses uses the expression 'in the last days' (באחרית הימים) and warns the people about what will happen to them, in a similar way that Jacob gathers his sons.
Isaiah prophesies about what will happen 'in the last days' (באחרית הימים), a key expression also used by Jacob.
By faith, Jacob blessed each of Joseph's sons as he lay on his deathbed, referring to Jacob's actions at the end of his life.
The summary of Jacob's blessings over his twelve sons, which provides context for the entire chapter that begins in verse 1.
Both verses describe Jacob's final great gatherings where, as the patriarch, he passes God's promises and blessings to his sons before his death.
The verses illuminate each other by showing Jacob's reaction to Simeon and Levi's violence: first as a fear of destruction, later as a prophetic judgment over their character.
Both verses are death prophecies where the patriarchs confirm God's promise to lead the people out of Egypt into the promised land.
